name: Amanta Healthcare Ltd
title: Amanta Healthcare Ltd - 544502 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Capacity doubling from 6.6 to ~12 crore bottles (SteriPort line 3) due ~20 June; management targets 24-25% EBITDA margin, but commissioning, 4-month polymer buffer and inventory build point to a slow ramp.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue INR288 crore (up ~5%), EBITDA INR63 crore at ~22% margin, PAT up 42%; SteriPort capacity expansion targeted operational by 20 June 2026.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR288 crore, up about 5%, with EBITDA of INR63 crore at a stable ~22% margin and PAT up over 42% YoY, driven mainly by lower finance cost. Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR77 crore (up 6.8% on the stated basis) and Q4 PAT was INR5.5 crore, up 28% YoY. The SteriPort ISBM capacity expansion (6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year) is not yet contributing and is guided to start by 20 June 2026. Management guided to 24-25% blended EBITDA margin going forward, with SteriPort at ~27%, and said polymer cost increases of 60-70% are being passed through with a ~INR2 per bottle impact.

financial_highlights.change: PAT up over 42% YoY; PAT margin up ~100 bps
6.8% growth as stated on a YoY basis
management expects to fall by about half to INR10-12 crore, per analyst's question; not disputed

financial_highlights.value: INR234 crore at 31 March 2026; INR204 crore as of call date
financial_highlights.change: Bajaj Finance refinancing done early April
expected to fall to single digit

segments.name: SteriPort (two-port ISBM IV fluid)
segments.commentary: Contributes nearly 42% of revenue from operations. Expansion from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year; management expects ~INR110-120 crore annual revenue and ~26-27% EBITDA margin at full run-rate.

segments.name: SVP (small volume parenterals)
segments.commentary: Inhalation solutions and preservative-free ophthalmics are ~20% of SVP revenue in FY26. New SVP line expected commissioning in October-December 2026; ophthalmic and inhalation products targeted for commercialisation in FY27-28.

segments.name: Ophthalmics
segments.commentary: Among the smallest SBUs; 70-80% of its revenue comes from the UK. Growth is product-development led (preservative-free classic pack in development), not capex-led.

guidance_outlook: SteriPort expansion expected to be operational by 20 June 2026 (stage-2 trial ~5 June, validation ~15 days); management kept a ~10-day buffer.
Management expects three full quarters of SteriPort contribution in FY27, with ~INR80-85 crore incremental revenue in year one.
Blended EBITDA margin expected at 24-25% going forward (existing ~22%, SteriPort ~27%); management described 25%+ as achievable once new capacity is sold out.
PAT margin of 5-6% seen as sustainable short term; expected to improve by at least 3% once operating leverage is fully realised, with PAT growing faster than EBITDA and sales.
Solar project (10.8 MW captive) expected to save ~INR75 lakh per month from about 25-30 May 2026 (per management's cost-saving view).
Plan to refinance a further INR30-40 crore of debt at lower rates within six months.
capex_capacity: SteriPort ISBM capacity being expanded from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year; all equipment installed, stage-wise commissioning and Italian-engineer trials complete; mopping-up ongoing.

Management expects to run at 95-100% of the new capacity from day one, assuming 20 operating hours versus 24 for BFS; separately, an analyst's question on 90-92% utilisation was answered affirmatively in the call.
Inventory build expected in the first quarter after expansion; equilibrium in three to four months, with a 9-10 month cycle to normalise inventory.
New SVP line expected commissioning in October-December 2026.
State FDA plant-plan approval already obtained for SteriPort Line 3; state inspection expected to take about one week after full commissioning, running in parallel with validation.
demand_pricing: Polymer (PE/PP) input prices up roughly 60-70%; impact estimated at INR1.25-1.75 per container, or about INR2 per SteriPort bottle; management said selling prices have been revised and it expects to be broadly neutral, with the price correction slightly above cost increase because packaging, films and transport costs are also rising.
Price revision initiated about 20-25 days before the call with no customer resistance reported; for a 100 ml container the price increase is about 5.5-6% of selling price.

Management said power costs have fallen because of solar, and that polymer price pass-through typically lags, with price cuts on reversal expected to be partial (e.g., INR2 rise may reverse by INR0.75-1).

Indian IV fluid demand growing 8-10% YoY, ~INR185 crore market per management's estimate; two-port segment expected to grow 12-13%. SteriPort demand estimated at 20-25 crore bottles, rising to 75-80 crore bottles by 2030; management targets 20-25% share.
Export order visibility is about three to six months; East Africa purchases concentrated in September-March; no order book spanning a year.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing raw material price and supply pressure, and will gross margins be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds a four-month polymer buffer (up from three), sources mainly from South Korea, and says it has passed on the cost increase; it said gross margin should be unaffected, and the benefit of lower-cost inventory is expected in Q1 FY27 rather than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will hospitals downgrade from SteriPort to cheaper products given price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR2 per-bottle increase is immaterial given nursing-home charges of INR500-1,500 per bottle administered, and that no price resistance has been seen; it cited no compliance-related customer audit requirement for SteriPort beyond state FDA plan approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost outlook and debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of borrowings are now in single-digit interest; CRISIL rating improved one notch to BBB; management expects to replace INR30-40 crore more debt at lower rates in six months and to repay debt from cash flows; total debt INR234 crore at March 2026 fell to INR204 crore as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue and margin should be expected from SteriPort in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed ~INR80-85 crore incremental revenue in FY27 from three quarters of operation (versus ~INR110-120 crore full year), and ~26-27% EBITDA margin for SteriPort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and receivables outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle is 120-125 days, targeted to ~110 days; receivables improved as old government and export dues were recovered and customers paid early ahead of price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and top markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were ~39% of FY26 revenue versus 32% in FY25; top markets include Thailand, UK, Philippines and South Sudan, with products marketed in 25-30 countries.

risks_watch: Commissioning slippage: SteriPort operational date of 20 June 2026 depends on stage-2 trials, validation and state FDA inspection.
Inventory build and ramp-up after expansion could pressure pricing and working capital in the first two to three quarters.
Polymer prices are volatile; management expects a lagged and partial price reversal, which could hurt margins as inventory is re-priced.
Competition in two-port systems (e.g., Eurohead-type products from other companies); management said these must demonstrate collapsibility to get the same NPPA pricing.
Contract structures with hospital chains are one-sided, and the company does not sign long-term contracts; order visibility is only three to six months.
Company declined to give the split of domestic sales between large hospital chains and standalone hospitals; a quantified order visibility figure for next quarter was promised later.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and margins, with a clear focus on execution timelines; somewhat evasive on quantification (order book, hospital-chain revenue mix, Eurohead competitor details, and debt rating), and management promised to share some data separately.
key_quotes: So we are hopeful that by 20th June we should be able to get operational.
So combining the new and the existing, on an average basis we will be expecting between 24% to 25% EBITDA margin going forward.
We have yet to receive a single complaint of fungal contamination.
So on the same capacity what we were having last year, we are able to register a decent growth. It speaks about our resilience.

adds.what: SteriPort ISBM capacity expansion 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles/yr (Line 3)

growth.why: SteriPort capacity expansion from 6.6 to ~12 crore bottles/yr, guided operational by 20 June 2026 with ~INR80-85 crore incremental FY27 revenue across three full quarters, backed by installed equipment and state FDA plant-plan approval; FY26 revenue up ~5% and Q4 up 6.8%, with 24-25% blended EBITDA margin guided.
